stem: Meher multiplies a 3-digit whole number by a 2-digit whole number. She wants the possible digit count of the product before multiplying every case.

parts.text: Which claim correctly states the possible digit counts?

options.text: The product always has exactly $6$ digits.
The product can have $4$ digits or $5$ digits.
The product always has exactly $2$ digits.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: The least 3-digit times least 2-digit is $100\times10=1000$ (4 digits); the greatest is $999\times99=98901$ (5 digits), so the product has 4 or 5 digits.

teacher.key_rationale: An m-digit times an n-digit product has m+n-1 or m+n digits. Here that is 4 or 5, not a fixed 6 or a fixed 2.
